correctness.rationale: For m≥3, the graph has 2m+2 vertices, 3m edges, degree-m poles and degree-2 internal vertices; distances: d(p,q)=3; d(a_i,a_j)=d(b_i,b_j)=2 for i≠j, d(a_i,b_i)=1, d(a_i,b_j)=3 for i≠j, every pole to every internal vertex ≤2. Thus at scale 1 the Rips complex is the original connected triangle-free graph with cycle rank m−1. At scale 2 it is exactly S^0*L_m where L_m comprises two full disjoint simplices (on the a and b layers) plus m matched bridges; quotient of two contractible disjoint subcomplexes yields the m-edge banana graph, L_m≃∨^(m−1)S^1, suspension gives ∨^(m−1)S^2 and torsionfree integral homology. Diameter 3 gives a simplex at scale≥3 and no intermediate changes; reduced bars are (2m+1)×[0,1) in H0, (m−1)×[1,2) in H1, (m−1)×[2,3) in H2. Integral H1 of oriented pole-to-pole arms is the augmentation lattice with pole swap −1. H1(L_m) is augmentation on oriented a-to-b bridges with flip −1; H~0(S0) flip −1; the join tensor yields pole flip +1 on H2 and natural coordinate permutation S_m. For m≥3 the two poles alone have valence m≥3, identifying the entire Aut group as S_m×C2. A separate independent BFS/face enumeration and mod-2 reduction for m=3..6 plus 144 signed Lefschetz cases agreed after applying the correct (−1)^k homological Lefschetz convention. Finite checks corroborate, not prove, the uniform statements.
residual_risks: Proof applies only to equal unweighted length-three branches, graph vertices (not continuous metric realizations), m≥3, inclusive threshold without factor-of-two rescaling.
The finite tests are not a formal proof for all m and do not verify every possible coefficient system.

value.rationale: Natural, nontrivial complete integral Rips persistence invariant for an unbounded canonical theta-graph family at precisely the girth-six boundary outside general girth≥7 stabilization; its binomial(m,2) six-cycles share entire three-edge arms so disjoint-cycle methods fail. Exact all-scale wedge types, field-independent torsionfree barcodes and complete integral S_m×C2 actions give a useful structural test example. Especially the pole flip changes from −1 on degree-one cycles to +1 on degree-two spheres although Betti ranks match, a distinction not encoded in previously published nonequivariant sphere enumerations. This claim does not claim a general classification for all girth-six graphs or unequal path lengths.
residual_risks: The proof is an elementary join/augmentation calculation; do not overstate a general-purpose homological theory or downstream result.
Novelty is necessarily best-of-knowledge and can be revised by an equivalent unindexed theorem.
